email_subject: Senior Backend Engineer Application -- Asha Verma (Java/Spring, Python, Kubernetes)
opening: The hardest problem I have enjoyed solving was untangling a monolithic batch service that had outgrown its design. At [Company], the work behind [Role] reads like the kind of backend engineering I want to do for the next decade, and [why-this-company] is what made me reach out.
body: Over six years I have built backend systems in Java/Spring and Python that hold up under real production pressure. My most consequential project re-architected that monolith into decoupled microservices on Kubernetes and migrated it with zero downtime across two consecutive releases -- which mattered more to the business than any single feature.

Reliability is a habit, not a one-off. I designed SLA-based alerting and self-healing retries, added readiness probes for zero-downtime rolling updates, and delivered a secrets-rotation integration with least-privilege IAM. Earlier, at Globex Systems, I cut CI build time ~55% and cloud cost ~30% while owning REST APIs for 40+ enterprise clients.

The modern edge I bring is AI applied pragmatically to engineering itself: an internal test-generation agent that produced ~20,000 lines of tests across 40+ modules at near-zero added cost. Outside work I maintain open source, including PromptForge, an LLM prompt toolkit with 300+ tests.
closing: I would welcome the chance to talk through how I would approach [Role] and where I could contribute fastest. I am open to relocation and can work across time zones. Thank you for reading.
why_company_prompt: Replace [why-this-company] with one specific, recent detail about [Company] that genuinely draws you: a backend/platform engineering blog post, an open-sourced library, or a scale/reliability challenge they have written about. Avoid generic praise like "industry leader" -- name the concrete thing and why it resonates.
notes_md:
- Use for backend / Senior Software Engineer roles where Java/Spring or Python + microservices + reliability are the core ask; AI is a bonus, not the headline.
- Customize: fill [Company], [Role], and especially [why-this-company] with a concrete, verifiable detail. Drop the relocation line if the role is local/remote.
- Tone: confident and warm; let the exact numbers (zero downtime, ~55%, ~30%, 40+ clients) carry the weight. Keep numbers exact and ASCII.
- ~300 words across short paragraphs. If a recruiter prefers brevity, cut the open-source sentence first.

email_subject: AI/GenAI Application Engineer -- Asha Verma (agentic LLM tooling, RAG, production backend)
opening: When I handed my coding standards to an internal test-generation agent, it produced ~20,000 lines of tests across 40+ modules and cut manual QA effort ~70% -- with zero production incidents. That convinced me the next leap in software is not bigger models but tighter, well-instructed agents wired into real workflows. It is also why [Role] at [Company] caught my attention: [why-this-company].
body: Those agents lifted coverage at near-zero added cost because I reused existing authenticated model sessions rather than provisioning new spend. I extended the same pattern into a multi-provider prompt toolkit adopted across three teams and a retrieval-augmented (RAG) layer over an internal knowledge base that cut support escalations ~25%. The throughline is turning LLMs from chat toys into dependable, auditable teammates.

I also build in the open: PromptForge is a multi-provider LLM prompt toolkit with 300+ tests, and AgentKit collects reusable AI-agent skills. Shipping these end to end keeps me honest about prompt design, evaluation, and the unglamorous reliability work production GenAI actually demands.

Underneath the AI sits real backend and cloud credibility: Java/Spring and Python services, microservice re-architecture on Kubernetes with zero downtime, and CI/CD discipline. I would love to bring this agent-first, cost-disciplined approach to [Company], and I am happy to relocate for the right team.
closing: Thanks for reading -- I would welcome the chance to walk through any of this in more detail, and I look forward to hearing from you.
why_company_prompt: Replace [why-this-company] with one or two concrete reasons you want THIS employer: a product, an AI/LLM initiative, an eng-blog post, or an open-source project, tied to agentic tooling, GenAI applications, or developer productivity. Avoid generic praise -- reference something only someone who researched the company would know.
notes_md:
- Use when the target role centers on AI/GenAI/LLM application engineering, agentic tooling, or developer-productivity AI -- not generic backend roles.
- Customize: fill [Company], [Role], and [why-this-company] with a researched, product-specific hook; if the JD names a stack (LangChain, a specific vector DB), mirror it.
- Lead with the test-gen agent result; it is the strongest, most quantified proof for this archetype. Keep the open-source paragraph if the company values builders.
- Tone: confident and specific, warm not boastful; relocation mentioned once. Keep numbers exact and ASCII.
